TIP 1: Bid rigging at Tal al-Zaytoun under Deputy CEO
CHANNEL: encrypted email (ProtonMail)
RECEIVED: 02 February 2026

I write as a former Contracts Manager for Tal al-Zaytoun Development Holdings Limited, a position I held from 02 February 2022 until my resignation on 14 November 2024. I have weighed this carefully and I cannot in good conscience remain silent about what I observed.

The Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Bashar Hijazi, established and maintained over the period of my employment a system of bid rigging that benefitted three preferred contractors and his own private interests. The mechanism was the following:

— Tender specifications were drafted by Hijazi's office in coordination with a Jordanian intermediary based in Amman, Ramzi Atwan, who relayed them to the favoured bidders before publication.
— Favoured bidders submitted compliant proposals at pre-agreed prices that contained margins between 18 and 24 percent above market rates.
— The price differential was distributed: a portion to Atwan as facilitation fee, a portion repatriated to Hijazi via a Cyprus-registered entity called Kavala Trading Limited.

The total volume of contracts processed under this system during my tenure, by my reconstruction of the procurement files, was USD 41,300,000. The estimated personal benefit accruing to Hijazi over the same period was approximately USD 2,400,000.

I retained, before my departure, copies of fourteen tender award files including the marked technical evaluations and the corresponding correspondence with Atwan. I did not retain originals. The copies are with me. I am willing to provide them through whatever channel you specify.

I would ask that any contact with me be initiated via this address only and that no third parties be informed of my identity until we have established a working understanding. May Allah grant you the courage to act.

TIP 2: Revenue recognition and capex irregularities, Tal al-Zaytoun
CHANNEL: encrypted email
RECEIVED: 18 October 2025

I am submitting this anonymously. I am a senior auditor at a Big Four firm and have done preparatory diligence work on the Tal al-Zaytoun project for two separate prospective investors over the past 18 months. I am breaching client confidentiality in writing this and I will not identify myself or my firm.

The pattern that has emerged from both engagements concerns the project's revenue recognition and capital expenditure reporting. There appear to be material discrepancies between the figures presented to investors in confidential information memoranda and the figures that would be supported by an independent reconstruction of the project's books from underlying transaction data.

Specifically:

(1) Construction-in-progress is reported on the project's internal financials at a value approximately 14–18% above what would be supported by an arm's-length valuation of completed and partially completed assets. The over-reporting concentrates in three building phases handled by contractors I will not name in this submission.

(2) Pre-sale residential revenue is being recognized in periods inconsistent with the underlying customer contracts. Specifically, deposits received under reservation agreements that contain refund clauses are being recognized as revenue, which under IFRS 15 they should not be.

(3) Land valuation: there are inconsistencies between the values at which land parcels were acquired (per registry filings) and the values at which the same parcels are carried on the project's balance sheet. The differential, in aggregate, is approximately $11 million favorable to the project.

The cumulative effect is that the project is presented to investors as more capital-efficient and more cash-positive than its underlying operations support. This is a securities concern (for the Gulf investors), a tax concern (for the PA), and an audit concern (for whichever firm is signing the project's accounts).

I do not know the names of the individuals responsible. The pattern is established at the level of accounting policy and approval workflow. The CEO and CFO would necessarily be aware. I am submitting this because the pattern is unlikely to be visible from outside the audit context but is straightforward to confirm with appropriate access.

TIP 3: Suspicious wire transfers from Tal al-Zaytoun operational account
CHANNEL: Telegram (one-way bot)
RECEIVED: 04 February 2026

I work in the finance department of Tal al-Zaytoun Development Holdings. I cannot give my role specifically because doing so would identify me. I have weighed this carefully before writing.

There is a name that should be at the centre of any investigation of corruption at this project: Bashar Hijazi, the Deputy CEO. The picture is becoming clear and I want to add what I know.

On 03 March 2024 a transfer of USD 1,150,000 was executed from our operational account to a Cyprus entity, Kavala Trading Limited, against an invoice for "advisory services on regional partnership development." There is no advisory services contract on file. The invoice was approved by Hijazi alone, bypassing the dual-signature requirement.

On 07 August 2024 a similar transfer of USD 1,250,000 was executed to the same entity against an invoice for "market study deliverables." Again no underlying contract is on file. Again Hijazi's approval alone.

The two transfers together total USD 2,400,000 and correspond exactly to what I have been told other staff are also reporting about Hijazi's personal benefit from this project.

The intermediary in these transfers — based on what is referenced in the wire instructions — is connected to a Jordanian fixer named Ramzi Atwan, whose name has come up in other contexts in this office.

I have screenshots of the transfer authorisations, the invoices, and the wire instructions. I will provide them when we have a secure channel agreed.

Please protect my identity. I am still in this office.

والسلام عليكم.

TIP 4: Subcontractor's account of forced "facilitation" payments
CHANNEL: postal mail (translated from Arabic)
RECEIVED: 06 February 2026

To Mr. Fadi Elsalameen, after greetings:

I write you these words from one who has lost much and gained little in his dealings with Tal al-Zaytoun Development. I am the owner of a small construction subcontracting company that worked on three of the project's residential phases between 2022 and 2024. I have weighed this carefully before writing.

The story is brief but instructive. Our company submitted competitive bids for fourteen tender packages over those years. We were awarded three. In each of the three, after award, we were informed that we were required to engage a "facilitation consultant" — a Jordanian named Ramzi Atwan — at a cost equivalent to 12 percent of the contract value. This was non-negotiable. We complied because we needed the work.

The total we paid to Atwan over the three contracts was USD 580,000. We have receipts for these payments, billed as "site logistics consulting" through a Jordanian company associated with him.

The eleven tenders we bid on and lost — all of them — were awarded to one of three contractors I will name to you privately. We have come to understand that those three contractors had similar arrangements but at higher rates and with the resulting price loaded into the tender amounts approved by the Deputy CEO, Mr. Bashar Hijazi.

I have spoken with two other subcontractors who can attest to similar experiences. They are willing to come forward but want to see how my own approach to you is received first.

I am sending this through the post because the digital channels are not safe in our country.

May Allah preserve you and grant you success in your work.

TIP 5: Gulf investor restructuring and CEO behavior at Tal al-Zaytoun
CHANNEL: secure drop
RECEIVED: 12 April 2026

Hi. I work at the Tal al-Zaytoun project in community relations. Been there since the start basically, summer of 2022.

Reason I'm writing is what's been going on with the Gulf investor side and how the CEO Khalil Mansour personally has been handling it. Some of this might be widely known but maybe not the specifics.

There's a Saudi-side investor partnership that's supposed to be 23% equity. The deal was restructured in late 2023 in a way that nobody on our side really understood at the time. Mansour led the renegotiation himself, with only his executive assistant in the room. Came back saying we'd "improved the structure." What actually happened, based on what I've pieced together from the legal team since, is that a chunk of the project's commercial revenue rights — like, future rental income on the retail component — got carved out and assigned to a Saudi-controlled SPV. Not the core equity, the cash flow.

So on paper the deal looks the same. In reality the project gives away way more than it gets. The CEO came out fine — there's something about an "advisory fee" he received personally from the Saudi side after closing that nobody in the project office can really explain. Couple of million dollars, I've heard.

The other thing is the procurement side has been reshuffled three times in 18 months. Every time the new procurement head ends up reporting directly to Mansour rather than through normal channels. People who've raised flags have been moved out.

I don't have documents. I have what I've heard from colleagues over coffee and in meetings. If you think this is worth pursuing I can introduce you to two people who do have documents.

Anyway. Just wanted to put this out there.

TIP 6: Land acquisition fraud against Beit Reema families
CHANNEL: secure drop
RECEIVED: 07 February 2026

I am writing on behalf of three families from the village of Beit Reema whose lands were acquired for the Tal al-Zaytoun project under what we now believe were fraudulent valuations.

The lands in question — totalling approximately 47 dunams — were acquired between 11 May 2022 and 22 September 2022 at an aggregate price of USD 2,820,000, paid in three tranches via bank transfer. We accepted the valuation at the time on the basis of comparables presented to us by an intermediary named Ramzi Atwan, who represented himself as acting on behalf of the project.

We have since come into possession, through a relative who works in the Ramallah land registry, of the appraisal report that the project itself filed for these same parcels. That report values our lands at USD 6,750,000 — more than double what we received. The differential of approximately USD 3,930,000 represents value that was extracted from our families and, we believe, retained by individuals inside the project.

The signature on our acquisition file is that of Bashar Hijazi, the Deputy CEO of Tal al-Zaytoun Development Holdings. His office handled the entire negotiation. We have weighed our options carefully and have decided to bring this to your attention because we do not believe Palestinian institutions will protect us against a project of this scale.

We are prepared to share the acquisition documents, the registry appraisal, and our identification under appropriate protections. We are seven adults representing the three families. We have not yet retained legal counsel.

نسأل الله أن يهديكم لما فيه الخير.

TIP 7: Pattern of corruption at Tal al-Zaytoun centered on Deputy CEO
CHANNEL: Signal message
RECEIVED: 10 February 2026

أخي فادي

I left Tal al-Zaytoun three months ago. I worked there as senior planner. I am writing because I cannot stay silent.

The corruption at this project comes from one place — the office of the Deputy CEO, Bashar Hijazi. Everyone inside knows. The pattern is well established and has been operating for at least three years.

The mechanism involves a fixer in Amman called Ramzi Atwan who handles the payments and the placements. Hijazi controls which contractors win, which valuations are approved, which transfers go through. His personal share over the project's life so far, based on what I have seen and heard, is in the range of USD 2,400,000 — possibly more.

The project's CEO is largely ceremonial. The board does not look beyond the headline numbers. Hijazi is the operational power and the operational corruption.

I have weighed this carefully. I know the risks. But I also know that without external pressure nothing will change.

I have memos, internal calendar entries showing meetings with Atwan, and an email chain in which Hijazi instructs the procurement office to "process at the agreed structure." These I retained on personal devices.

I am willing to share when we have a channel agreed. Please keep my identity protected — Hijazi has reach inside our community.

May Allah strengthen you.
